title: A loyalty platform's own OAuth authorization server, serving a public mobile client and confidential partner apps
provenance: Synthetic system authored for this corpus (issue #744). Not derived from, or sanitized from, any real system: there is nothing to leak by omission.
notes: Holdout case 1 of 2 for #744. It fills three gaps at once: the corpus's first ASVS level 3 case, the first case where we run the OAuth authorization server ourselves, and the first where a session and a token are two different things with two different lifetimes. The central finding needs three stated facts no one sentence holds: the rewards API checks no audience, one key signs tokens for the API and for the support console, and the console sits on the same public hostname. Level 3 is what turns two stated values into gaps: a ten-minute authorization code and plain bearer tokens are both acceptable at level 2. Held out of tuning: no diagnosis reads it, so it confirms a fix measured on the other cases.
